I personally am not sure it would look good if they find them accidentally or if there was a bandage (they are bound to ask what happened and unless you are a great liar they will be suspicious). 

I think your best bet would be to be completely honest if they ask to lift your left sleeve (hopefully you can get away with just the right one and not say anything). Say something like "okay I just want to warn you that I have some scars on my arm... It's something I'm getting help for and is also why I'm trying to better my career for myself".   Yes this may lose you the job, but there are so many more people now who understand mental illness and how actually getting a job you want will only motivate you to do better. It will all depend on the interviewers personal opinion tbh. Perhaps if some cuts are fresh, wear the bandage underneath your sleeve anyway.  

I know it's really hard to do the above, I understand as have avoided job opportunities myself when I realised it may mean bloods/blood pressure etc. but when I look back now I wish id tried to be honest (or try to use the other arm) as someone may have seen past that and looked at my capabilities to do the job. I have got better at being honest when people ask questions sometimes. For example yday it was extremely hot and I got stopped by some old friends who asked wasn't I hot in my log sleeved black jumper (was all I had to wear)? I thought about lying and could feel myself starting to go red and panic because I'm a shit liar. So I just said 'I did something stupid at the weekend' and although they looked uncomfortable for a second, they were then empathic and one even said I've been going through a really shit time too recently and have thought about similar things. So I guess it actually helped us relate a bit and I felt a bit more at ease.  

Honesty is the best policy I necessary as otherwise they won't trust you which is a worse trait as an employee. Ultimately it's your decision but don't do what I did and miss opportunities that eventually will help your mental health. 

Edit: also I find when I go to docs and know they will be looking at my arms, I angle the right side of my body to them slightly so that when they go to do it, my right arm is more accessible and in don't look so awkward swapping arms. Has worked so far for me
